definition.name: AWS access key
definition.remediation: Deactivate this key in AWS IAM, create a new one, and load it from a secret manager or environment variable instead of the file.

definition.name: GitHub token
definition.remediation: Revoke this token in GitHub settings and create a new one with only the scopes it needs.

definition.name: Private key block
definition.remediation: Treat this key as compromised: replace it, revoke the old one, and keep private keys in a key store or secret manager.

definition.name: Secret-looking assignment
definition.remediation: If this is a real secret, rotate it and load it from a secret manager or environment variable instead of the file.

definition.name: Secret written to a log
definition.remediation: Remove the secret from this log call, or log a fixed placeholder such as "[redacted]" instead.

definition.name: npm token
definition.remediation: Revoke this token in your npm account's Access Tokens page and create a new one with only the permissions it needs.

definition.name: GitLab personal access token
definition.remediation: Revoke this token in GitLab (User settings, Access tokens) and create a new one with only the scopes it needs.

definition.name: GitLab personal access token (legacy format)
definition.remediation: Revoke this token in GitLab (User settings, Access tokens) and create a new one with only the scopes it needs.

definition.name: Payment card number
definition.remediation: Remove the card number. If it's real, treat it as exposed card data: tell your payment provider and follow your PCI DSS incident process.

definition.name: Bitcoin private key (WIF)
definition.remediation: Move any funds to a new wallet whose key has never been exposed. A leaked private key can't be revoked.

definition.name: Password-shaped value
definition.remediation: If this is a real password, change it, since it has been stored in plain text, and load the new one from a secret manager or environment variable. If it isn't a secret, this low-severity finding can be ignored.

definition.name: Slack token
definition.remediation: Revoke this token in your Slack app's settings (OAuth & Permissions), reinstall the app to get a new one, and load the new one from a secret manager or environment variable instead of the file.

definition.name: Slack webhook URL
definition.remediation: Anyone with this URL can post to the channel. Remove the webhook in your Slack app's Incoming Webhooks page, add a new one, and load the new one from a secret manager or environment variable instead of the file.

definition.name: Stripe live secret key
definition.remediation: Roll this key in the Stripe Dashboard (Developers, API keys) and load the new one from a secret manager or environment variable instead of the file.

definition.name: Stripe live restricted key
definition.remediation: Roll this key in the Stripe Dashboard (Developers, API keys) and load the new one from a secret manager or environment variable instead of the file.

definition.name: SendGrid API key
definition.remediation: Delete this key in SendGrid (Settings, API Keys), create a new one with only the permissions it needs, and load the new one from a secret manager or environment variable instead of the file.

definition.name: Google API key
definition.remediation: Delete or regenerate this key in Google Cloud Console (APIs & Services, Credentials), restrict the new one to the APIs and apps that need it, and load the new one from a secret manager or environment variable instead of the file.

definition.name: OpenAI API key
definition.remediation: Revoke this key in the OpenAI dashboard (API keys), create a new one, and load the new one from a secret manager or environment variable instead of the file.

definition.name: Anthropic API key
definition.remediation: Revoke this key in the Claude Console (API keys), create a new one, and load the new one from a secret manager or environment variable instead of the file.

definition.name: GitHub fine-grained token
definition.remediation: Revoke this token in GitHub settings (Developer settings, Fine-grained tokens) and create a new one with access to only the repositories and permissions it needs.

definition.name: AWS secret access key
definition.remediation: Deactivate the access key this secret belongs to in AWS IAM, create a new one, and load it from a secret manager or environment variable instead of the file.

definition.name: Sentry DSN
definition.remediation: A Sentry DSN is meant to be public in browser apps, but anyone who has it can send events to your project. If this DSN is for a server, create a new client key in Sentry (Project settings, Client Keys), disable this one, and load the DSN from config.

definition.name: Credentials in a URL
definition.remediation: Change this password, since it's stored in plain text, and build the URL at runtime from a password loaded from a secret manager or environment variable.

definition.name: Basic auth header
definition.remediation: This is a base64-encoded username and password, not an encrypted one. Change the password, and add the header at runtime from a secret manager or environment variable.

definition.name: Bearer token in a header
definition.remediation: If this token is still valid, revoke it with the service that issued it, and add the header at runtime from a secret manager or environment variable.

definition.name: JSON Web Token
definition.remediation: A signed JWT works as a credential until it expires. Invalidate the session it belongs to, rotate the signing key if the token is long-lived, and don't store tokens in files or logs.

definition.name: Password hash
definition.remediation: A password hash can be cracked offline. If it belongs to a real account, have that user change their password, and create seed or test users at runtime instead of storing their hashes in the file.

definition.name: Password in a SQL statement
definition.remediation: Change this database password, since it's stored in plain text, and set it at deploy time from a secret manager instead of the migration or script.

definition.name: Password in a connection string
definition.remediation: Change this database password, since it's stored in plain text, and load the connection string from a secret manager or environment variable instead of the file.

definition.name: Azure account or shared access key
definition.remediation: Rotate this key in the Azure portal (Access keys, or Shared access policies), and load the connection string from Key Vault or an environment variable instead of the file.

definition.name: JSON Web Key with private material
definition.remediation: This JWK holds a private or symmetric key (its "d" or "k" member). Treat it as compromised: replace it, remove it from your key set, and keep signing keys in a key store or secret manager.

definition.name: PuTTY private key
definition.remediation: Treat this key as compromised: remove its public key from every server's authorized keys, create a new key pair, and keep private keys out of the repository.

definition.name: Private key without PEM armor
definition.remediation: This is a base64 private key (RSA, EC, or Ed25519) with its PEM header removed. Treat it as compromised: replace it, revoke the old one, and keep private keys in a key store or secret manager.

definition.name: Keystore file in base64
definition.remediation: This is a PKCS#12 or Java keystore written as base64. Its password may be weak or stored nearby, so replace the keys it holds and keep the keystore in a secret manager instead of the file.

definition.name: Kubernetes Secret with inline data
definition.remediation: Values in a Secret's data are base64-encoded, not encrypted. Rotate every value in it, and keep the manifest out of the repository: create it from a secret manager (External Secrets) or commit it encrypted (Sealed Secrets, SOPS).

definition.name: Registry auth (base64 user and password)
definition.remediation: This is a base64-encoded username and password for a package or container registry (.npmrc, Docker config.json). Change the password or revoke the token, and log in at build time from a secret instead of committing the file.

definition.name: .netrc password
definition.remediation: Change this password or revoke the token, and keep .netrc files in the home directory with 600 permissions instead of in the repository or an image.

definition.name: Session cookie
definition.remediation: Anyone with this cookie can act as the signed-in user. End the session it belongs to, and remove it from the file or log.

definition.name: Pre-signed storage URL
definition.remediation: Anyone with this URL can use it until it expires. If it hasn't expired, revoke the credentials that signed it, and generate pre-signed URLs when they're needed instead of storing them.
